Definition: from G303 (in the sense of intensity) and πῆρος (maimed); crippled:--maimed.
BiblicalUsage: The word means maimed, crippled: when you make a feast, Jesus says, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind — and the servant reports that the master has ordered him to bring in the poor and the maimed and the halt and the blind. It appears only twice, both times in the same parable, and both times the maimed are the ones invited in off the streets.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for maimed carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the guest list — the poor, the maimed, the halt and the blind, brought in from the streets and lanes to fill the house.
